chapter: Cab Calloway, Haiti and Sarah Vaughan
title: Joining Cab Calloway's band in 1947
summary: Budd joins Calloway in Chattanooga replacing Rudy Powell, praises the organization, and gets a pink slip at the Capitol Theater.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: What was happening -- what year was that, Bud?
This was 1938.
1938, yeah.
That's right.
Yeah, that's interesting, because I -- I'm quite aware because I was traveling with Cab Calloway and we were sometimes --
But you guys were traveling in style.
Yeah, but it was still a kind of a rough thing. Also -- when did you join Cab, because I was in the band when you came in...
Oh, yes. Calloway's band. Well, you know, Cab sent for me to come down there, and it was in 1947. And I joined you in Chattanooga, Tennessee.
(Laughter)
Well, we were ______, but you joined in 1947.
1947 I joined Cab Calloway's band, and I took Mushi's place -- that's Rudy Powell.
Rudy Powell, which he changed his name to Musa Kaleem, Mushi Kaweem.
Yeah, Musa Kaleem, Mushi Kaweem.
That was at the beginning of the Muslim -- very beautiful alto sax, and I played alto sax, you

remember. And, of course, some of the parts was, on my part, a few first parts and everything. And you guys had a beautiful band. And, you know, I always think about that time that I joined Cab Calloway's band. You know, you were very well organized. You guys -- you remember Mr. Wright.
Yes. Our road manager.
(Simultaneous remarks)

And you guys were so well organized men, you know, and I thought it was kind of like a rebel, at least my brother, he didn't like for me to be runnin' off at the mouth so much, you know, like. And anyway, when I played with Cab, and we played our way back to New York City. And when we got to New York City, we went into this Strand Theater. Or was it the Capital Theater?
Yeah, one of them.
Capital Theater. That's right across the street backstage from Beefsteak Charlie's. Remember?
Right. Right.
And after I made my first week, I had my pay envelope, and in it was a pink slip.
(Laughter)
(Unintelligible).
Remember you got that pink slip, you didn't know was that your notice.
(Simultaneous remarks)
So one of the most interesting things that happened to me, -- Panama Francis was in the band. Sam the Man Taylor, Hilton Jefferson, who is a great man that I respected. He was actually --
I'm going to ask you about him in a minute.
